summary: Best state ea498c783e5bd552: 1.148x over the baseline (240 pairs, CI 1.146..1.151; 31.3 us against 35.9 us). Most of it is a source rewrite (state a3f1f14b4b217381, 1.116x at 60 pairs, credited to amdclang): each (value, index) pair is packed into one finite double (high word = float bits + 0x00100000, low word = ~index for positive values / index for negative ones), so a compare-exchange of the top-8 sorting network is v_max_f64 + v_min_f64 instead of v_cmp_gt_i64 + four v_cndmask (hot loop 276 -> 173 instructions). The machine-level gain on top of that amdclang build is 1.027x (compare, 240 pairs, CI 1.023..1.031): the next iteration's two x4 loads are issued at the top of the loop and waited one iteration later (branch-free, last iteration re-reads its own chunk through an s_cselect step), and the 16 `v_max_f64 x, x` sNaN canonicalizations amdclang emits per iteration are removed (operands are finite by construction). 1.5x was not reached: the kernel is at 31 us with about 20 us of launch, and already below the copy-model floor (headroom 0.89); the model is touched-once and the kernel reads logits exactly once, so this is the 'at the floor / launch-dominated' case, with the remaining time in per-CU ALU throughput rather than bytes.

friction: edit() text does not accept label lines ('bad mnemonic .Lpf31:'): a block cannot be split or a skip-branch added without resending the whole 800-instruction body through edit_ir. I had to express 'no prefetch on the last iteration' branch-free (s_cselect step) instead. An op like {op: 'split', block, index, label} or labels in edit text would fix it.
unroll_loads refused the whole kernel because a cold fallback path (k != 8) uses s_set_gpr_idx_on; the hot loop .LBB0_31 named in `loop` does not. The refusal should be scoped to the named loop.

amdclang inserts v_max_f64 x,x canonicalization on every fmax/fmin input coming from a bit_cast (16 per iteration here); there is no transform to drop canonicalizations the author can prove unnecessary, and removing them by hand needed register renaming across 12 instructions. A 'rename register in index range' edit op would make this a one-liner.

The memory-floor model (20 us launch + bytes/4.5 TB/s) reports headroom 0.89..0.97 for this kernel, i.e. it is already beyond the 'floor'; the headroom says 'memory-bound' while the block-1024 relaunch (0.46x) shows the kernel is bound by ALU throughput per CU. A probe that reports time with loads kept but ALU removed (or the reverse) would have told this directly.
No tool states the cost (cycles) of an instruction class: whether v_max_f64 costs more than a 32-bit VALU op had to be inferred from end-to-end timing.
lessons: A 64-bit (key, payload) compare-exchange can be two instructions: pack the pair into a finite double and use v_max_f64 / v_min_f64. For float keys: high word = bits(x + 0.0f) + 0x00100000 (keeps sign-magnitude order, never a double NaN/inf/denormal for non-NaN floats, including +-inf), low word = ~index for positive values and index for negative ones (lo = ~idx ^ (bits >> 31)); sentinel 0xff900000ffffffff decodes to value -inf, index -1. moe_gate_topk hot loop 276 -> 173 instructions, 1.12x end to end (kernel part about 15.9 -> 12.3 us after 20 us launch). Expressible in HIP with __builtin_fmax/__builtin_fmin on bit_cast doubles.

amdclang canonicalizes (v_max_f64 x, x) every fmax/fmin input it cannot prove non-sNaN: 16 extra f64 ops per iteration here. Removing them at machine level together with one-iteration-ahead load pipelining gave 1.027x (240-pair compare) on a 31 us kernel.

Software pipelining without a branch or a loop copy: keep the loop's own address register, prefetch from addr + (more_iterations ? stride : 0) computed with s_cmp + s_cselect_b32 and v_lshl_add_u64 v, v, 0, s[lo:hi]; the last iteration harmlessly re-reads its own chunk, no out-of-bounds read. Costs 4 v_mov_b64 per iteration to move the prefetched registers into place.

A headroom near 1.0 does not prove memory-bound on a 35 us kernel: relaunching with block 1024 (64 workgroups, 16 waves per CU) ran 0.46x, showing ALU throughput per CU was the bound; cutting 37 % of the loop instructions then paid 1.12x. Rough fit here: about 1.1 us per 1000 VALU instructions per wave (4 waves per CU, 256 CUs) on top of about 26 us.
Launch geometry for this kernel: block 256 (256 workgroups of 4 waves = one per CU) is best; block 64 parity (0.995) on the baseline, block 128 0.88x on the optimized state, block 1024 0.46x.

session.final:
The session is reported: the best state is `ea498c783e5bd552`, 1.148x over the baseline (240 pairs, CI 1.146–1.151; 31.3 us against 35.9 us). The 1.5x target was not reached, and the machine-level gain that counts is only about 1.027x.

- **Source level (credited to amdclang), 1.116x:** state `a3f1f14b4b217381` packs each (value, index) pair into one finite double, so a compare-exchange in the top-8 sorting network is `v_max_f64` + `v_min_f64` instead of a 64-bit compare and four selects. The hot loop drops from 276 to 173 instructions.
- **Machine level on top, 1.027x** (direct compare, 240 pairs, CI 1.023–1.031):
  - The next iteration's two x4 loads are issued at the top of the loop and waited one iteration later.
  - The 16 `v_max_f64 x, x` canonicalizations amdclang emits per iteration are removed.
- **Why not 1.5x:** about 20 us of the 31 us is launch, and the kernel reads the logits exactly once. It is already below the copy-model floor (headroom 0.89), so 1.5x would need 23 us total. What remains is per-CU arithmetic throughput, not bytes.

| `unroll_loads` on the baseline | refused: the cold `k != 8` path uses indexed registers |
